# SOP Audit: The Forge Belfast

## **Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member onboarding** – no documented first 7 days/30 days journey (assessment, intro class flow, expectation-setting, retention hooks)
- **Churn & cancellation handling** – no win-back protocol, exit interview process, or pause-vs-cancel decision tree
- **Coaching standards & quality assurance** – no class audit checklist, cue consistency framework, or feedback loop to coaches
- **Member check-in cadence** – no systematic touchpoint schedule (weeks 1, 4, 12) to catch drift early
- **Complaints & incidents** – no escalation protocol, documentation standard, or safeguarding/health emergency response
- **Finance controls** – no refund policy, payment failure handling, or reconciliation SOP
- **Data privacy/GDPR** – no member consent workflow, data retention, or breach response
- **Staffing continuity** – no staff induction, handover, or absence cover protocol
- **Marketing campaign execution** – no brief-to-launch workflow, asset approval, or performance review cadence

---

## **Needs updating**

- **Coach SOPs (21/24)** – missing the coaching development roadmap and weekly key tasks; no clarity on progression from hire → master coach
- **Client SOPs (28/37)** – milestone achievements, referral programme, and 30-day goals frameworks not documented; retention mechanics unclear
- **Member Outcomes** – no tracking standard or reporting template (how do we measure and communicate member progress?)
- **Troubleshooting Guide** – doesn't exist; should cover no-show patterns, class-fit issues, payment problems, and low engagement flags

---

## **Build next**

**1. Member Onboarding (Weeks 0–4)**

# Service Menu Build — Tactical Execute

• **Shadow your top 3 coaches THIS WEEK** — 90 minutes each. Document what they *actually* sell (not what you think they sell). You'll find inconsistencies that are costing you money. Use real language they use, not corporate jargon.

• **Price by outcome + time, not guesswork** — Pull your last 20 invoices. What did members actually pay for? Group them: 1-on-1 coaching, small group programs, nutrition add-ons. Now reverse-engineer: if a 1-on-1 session takes 60 mins prep + delivery, what margin do you need? Price accordingly, then test it.

• **Build TWO separate one-pagers** (not a novel):
  - **Coach version**: "Here's what you can sell, commission structure, what's included in your time, what costs extra"
  - **Member version**: "Here's our packages, what you get, when/how to book, FAQs"
  - Get feedback from 2 coaches + 5 members within 48 hours. Iterate once. Done.

• **Post it where it matters** — Printed A4 at reception + coach whiteboard. Digital version in your booking system AND email it to every member who's asked a pricing question in the last month. Track which format generates questions (that's your clarity gap).

• **Set a 30-day review checkpoint** — Are coaches consistently selling the same things? Are members confused about add-ons? One conversation with Grace + one coach = fix before month-end.

What's your current biggest pricing confusion point from members/coaches?

Interview 5–10 churned members immediately; identify the pattern and reverse it in November onward. Even 2% improvement = £300+/month retained.
- **Member value is down 27% (Aug £106 vs Sep £133).** This isn't just churn—people are downgrading or using fewer classes. Audit class attendance by member tier (unlimited vs 4/8 class) and upsell idle unlimited members into nutrition coaching, PT bundles, or merchandise at £25–50/head. Target: recover to £130+/member by December.

---
